newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares jump 1.5 pct at start of settlement.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares jump 1.5 pct at start of settlement.

text.p: Heavy buying by speculators and foreign financial institutions (FIIs) at the start of a new settlement period on Monday drove share prices to a higher close on the Delhi Stock Exchange, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 10.72 points higher at 739.28.
"Everybody was interested in creating fresh positions today as it was the first day of the new settlement period," a broker said.
Traders said speculative buying on hopes that the government might present a market-friendly budget also aided the recovery.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram is due to present the financial budget 1997/98 (April-March) on February 28.

"Optimistic buying by speculators on hopes that the government might announce some sops for the capital market in the forthcoming financial budget also fuelled the rise in prices," said Ashok Arya of brokers S.C. Gupta.
But brokers said the current rally could be short-lived.
"The rally in prices seems to be temporary as there was no specific change in the market fundamentals and the market might react soon," said another broker.

ACC was in the spotlight as it jumped 118.75 rupees, or 9.27 percent, to 1,398.75 on heavy buying by FIIs amid expectations that the government would give some incentives to the cement sector in the forthcoming budget, brokers said.
Reliance Industries closed 0.45 rupee higher at 273.95 as profit-taking wiped out most of the early gains. The share had surged to 276.50 in early trade on FIIs buying, brokers said.
Larsen and Toubro rose 8.55 rupees to 242.
State Bank of India edged 4.90 rupees higher to 272.10.
